quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must let other traffic go first if it is close enough to cause a crash.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let other traffic go first if it is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. You should be ready to stop, but you can continue if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must let the pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to go before pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let the pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must let pedestrians finish crossing. Always yield to pedestrians, especially when turning.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of the lane.
Signal about 100 feet before you turn.
Turn your front wheels left while you wait.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal about 100 feet before you turn.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This way, if another car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You drive faster before turning.
Traffic flows to the right.
Traffic flows to the left.

questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: You should always drive:

options.text: At the same speed as the cars around you.
At the speed limit.
At a safe speed for the road and weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a safe speed for the road and weather.
questions.explanation: Your speed should fit the road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never exceed the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly both ways.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate. After the gate rises, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain your speed. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle safely move back into your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles.
Change lanes suddenly without planning.
Check if other vehicles are moving into the same lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:

options.text: One-third.
One-quarter.
One-half.

questions.explanation: Cut your normal speed in half when driving on packed snow. Use snow tires or chains on snowy roads.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night—they can blind you. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging from another road. Give them extra space to merge safely.
Traffic is merging from another road. Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from another road. Give them extra space to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will merge into your lane. Check your mirrors and move to another lane if you can. This gives merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: Stay farther behind other cars at night when it is harder to see. Use your headlights correctly. Never look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield the right-of-way to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrived. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right goes first.

questions.question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat the intersection like a stop sign.
May not proceed until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat the intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light the same as a stop sign. Stop completely at the line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller cars. If you stop suddenly in front of one, the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right.

questions.question: Bright headlights from an oncoming car are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your car on the road safely until you pass the oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: When you pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see clearly. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: You must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your windows. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you drive.

questions.question: You have a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: If no one is injured or killed and it is safe to do so, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane.
